high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary responsibilities and resources. Worries readily occupy my attention. A routine uncertainty can keep returning to mind while I try to do something else, and I can become caught up in my own problems after I have already done what is practical. Events that have ended may still leave me worrying about what happened.

I often anticipate what could go badly. Before an ordinary appointment or unfamiliar activity, frightening possibilities can come to mind without a clear warning. I can fear the worst rather than simply leaving the outcome open, and many different everyday situations can make me afraid.

I get stressed easily by interruptions and small complications. An event that others find manageable can disturb me, and I may stay bothered by a minor inconvenience. This describes tension and anxious disturbance rather than a necessary wish to argue or a belief that I cannot cope.

Feeling relaxed is less common for me, including during quiet parts of the day. A changed routine can take time to feel settled even once I understand it. These tendencies have exceptions: I can still act competently, enjoy company, recover from setbacks, and have good days. My mood, sociability, interests and ability vary independently; no clinical diagnosis or constant crisis is implied.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary responsibilities and resources. Everyday uncertainties generally do not keep me worrying for long. After I have done what I can about a problem, I can usually turn my attention elsewhere, and a completed event seldom remains a source of repeated worry. I can remember a mistake without staying caught up in it.

I do not ordinarily expect the worst just because an outcome is unknown. A new activity or routine appointment may leave some questions open without making me afraid. Fear is not a prominent response across many harmless situations, although a particular real danger can still concern me.

Small complications rarely disturb me much. A delay or interruption usually feels manageable without quickly making me stressed, and I am not easily bothered by ordinary events. This does not require me to be pleased with every inconvenience or incapable of anger.

I feel relaxed through much of an ordinary day and generally settle into changed situations fairly readily. A new routine can become comfortable without a long period of tension. These tendencies have exceptions: I can still make mistakes, dislike an activity, need practical help, and have difficult days. My mood, sociability, interests and ability vary independently; ease does not guarantee competence, happiness, or a perfect life.
